summary: count returns the number of non-overlapping substring occurrences.
documentation: count returns the number of non-overlapping substring occurrences. Matching is case-sensitive. An empty substring follows a special boundary-counting rule, so a nonempty search term is often clearer for business tasks.
inputs: A substring, optionally restricted by start/end bounds.
caution: Overlapping occurrences are not counted separately. For example, aa appears twice, not three times, in aaaa.
scenarios: Count repeated placeholders before filling a receipt.
Measure occurrences of a literal label in an imported note.
Check how often a delimiter token appears in a record.
title: Count non-overlapping tokens
problem: Input has text and token strings; token is nonempty. Return the number of non-overlapping exact token occurrences in text. Case matters.
goal: Use str.count() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Count literal occurrences; do not slide into overlapping matches.
